summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of complex migraines, sclerosing mesenteritis, and gastrostomy status was admitted for a severe migraine with aura, which was resistant to standard treatment. Imaging showed no acute intracranial pathology, and transient aphasia and left-sided weakness were attributed to her migraine pattern. During admission, she was found to have an ileus, likely related to her history of bowel dysmotility, which was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and symptom control. Her headache and ileus gradually improved over several days. The G-tube site required recannulation due to loosened sutures. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with her neurologist for Botox injection and to resume her missed iron infusion, with instructions to monitor for recurrence of neurological or abdominal symptoms.
problems: Migraine with aura, intractable, without status migrainosus
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
